title.zh: 种族和谐维护（限制令）条例 2026
title.en: Maintenance of Racial Harmony (Restraining Orders) Regulations 2026

completenessNote: 全文，共 18 条；逐字取自新加坡法规在线（SSO）官方打印视图，未改写、未节选。

text.en: 1. These Regulations are the Maintenance of Racial Harmony (Restraining Orders) Regulations 2026 and come into operation on 15 September 2026.

3.—(1) A document to be filed under these Regulations must —
(a)be addressed to the “Secretary, Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony”; and
(b)be sent —
(i)by email to PCRRH_Secretariat@mha.gov.sg; or
(ii)by registered post to the PCRRH Secretariat, Ministry of Home Affairs, New Phoenix Park, 28 Irrawaddy Road, Singapore 329560.
(2) When a document is filed by a party, the secretary must —
(a)serve a copy of the document on the other party; and
(b)send a copy of the document to every member.

4.—(1) A document to be served on a representor must be sent to the email address for service stated in the representations.
(2) A document to be served on the Minister must be sent to the email address for service stated in the Minister’s response filed under regulation 7(1).

5.—(1) A restrained person may file representations in accordance with section 33(3) and this regulation.
(2) The representations must state —
(a)the name and address of the representor (X);
(b)the name and address of each authorised representative of X, if any; and
(c)an email address for the service of documents.
(3) The representations must include a copy of the restraining order.
(4) Subject to any directions given by the Council, the representations must —
(a)present the relevant facts and issues;
(b)state the grounds for objecting to the restraining order, including —
(i)any alleged error of fact or law;
(ii)whether X is objecting to the whole or part of the restraining order; and
(iii)if X is objecting to part of the restraining order — the part that X objects to;
(c)present the arguments supporting each of those grounds; and
(d)include all affidavits or other documents supporting those arguments.
(5) If X proposes to call witnesses to give oral evidence, the representations must, for each proposed witness —
(a)state his or her —
(i)full name;
(ii)identity card number, passport number or work pass number; and
(iii)nationality and date of birth; and
(b)give a description of the evidence proposed to be given and the relevance of that evidence.
(6) If X intends to request the Council to make any directions, the representations must state the directions sought by X.
(7) The representations must be signed and dated by X or any authorised representative of X.

6.—(1) Representations may be amended only if the Council permits or directs the representor to do so.
(2) The Council may direct any representations to be amended if the Council considers the representations to be materially incomplete, unduly lengthy, or unclear.
(3) The Council must not permit an amendment to any representations to add a new ground of objection unless the Council is satisfied that —
(a)the ground is based on any matter of fact or law that came to light after the representations were filed;
(b)it was not practicable to include the ground when filing the representations; or
(c)there are exceptional circumstances.

7.—(1) The Minister may file a response to any representations in accordance with this regulation.
(2) The response must be filed within 5 working days after the date on which the Minister receives a copy of the representations.
(3) The response must state —
(a)the name and email address of each authorised officer, if any;
(b)the case number; and
(c)an email address for the service of documents.
(4) Subject to any directions given by the Council, the response —
(a)must contain a concise statement of the facts;
(b)must succinctly present the arguments of fact or law that the Minister will rely on;
(c)must include all affidavits or other documents supporting those arguments; and
(d)must not raise any new ground, fact or document that was not contained in the grounds, facts and documents given under section 33(1)(b).
(5) If the Minister proposes to call witnesses to give oral evidence, the response must, for each proposed witness —
(a)state his or her —
(i)full name;
(ii)identity card number, passport number or work pass number; and
(iii)nationality and date of birth; and
(b)give a description of the evidence proposed to be given and the relevance of that evidence.
(6) If the Minister intends to request the Council to make any directions, the response must state the directions sought by the Minister.
(7) The response must be signed and dated by the Minister or any authorised officer.

8.—(1) If the Minister files a response, the representor (X) may file a reply in accordance with this regulation.
(2) The reply must be filed within 2 working days after the date on which X receives the copy of the Minister’s response.
(3) The reply —
(a)must contain the arguments of fact or law in reply to the Minister’s response;
(b)must include all affidavits or other documents supporting those arguments; and
(c)must not raise any new ground of objection against the restraining order.
(4) The reply must be signed and dated by X or any authorised representative of X.

9.—(1) After the Council receives a restraining order —
(a)it must as soon as practicable give directions to the parties about how it intends to review the restraining order; and
(b)it may continue to give such directions as required.
(2) The directions must indicate —
(a)whether the Council intends to hear oral evidence and if so, how it intends to conduct the hearing; and
(b)whether the Council requires any further information or documents from the parties.
(3) The directions may include directions for the confidential treatment of any material that a party intends to rely on or is required to file.
(4) If a party fails to comply with any direction given by the Council, the Council may exclude the party from further involvement in the proceedings.

10.—(1) The Council may by written notice require any person in Singapore to provide any document or information to the Council.
(2) A person who is given a notice under paragraph (1) commits an offence if —
(a)the person fails to comply with the notice without reasonable excuse; or
(b)the person destroys, damages, alters or falsifies any document or information that the person is required to provide.
(3) However, the person is not required to provide any document or information that is subject to any privilege under any law or rule of professional conduct.
(4) A person who is guilty of an offence under paragraph (2) shall be liable on conviction —
(a)in relation to paragraph (2)(a), to a fine not exceeding $2,000; and
(b)in relation to paragraph (2)(b), to a fine not exceeding $10,000.

11.—(1) The Council may hear oral evidence, but is not required to do so.
(2) The Council may by written notice require any person in Singapore to give oral evidence at a specified time and place.
(3) The Council may allow a party to call witnesses to give oral evidence, but is not required to do so.
(4) The Council may require oral evidence to be given on oath.
(5) The Council may give directions on the examination, cross‑examination and re-examination of witnesses.
(6) The Council may allow a witness to give oral evidence using a live video link.
(7) The Council may appoint one or more interpreters and translators to assist the Council.
(8) A person who is given a written notice under paragraph (2) commits an offence if —
(a)the person fails to comply with the notice without reasonable excuse;
(b)in proceedings before the Council, the person refuses to answer any question put to him or her; or
(c)in proceedings before the Council, the person knowingly gives any evidence that is false or misleading.
(9) Paragraph (8)(b) does not apply if the refusal to answer is justified by any privilege under any law or rule of professional conduct.
(10) A person who is guilty of an offence under paragraph (8) shall be liable on conviction —
(a)in relation to paragraph (8)(a), to a fine not exceeding $2,000;
(b)in relation to paragraph (8)(b), to a fine not exceeding $5,000; and
(c)in relation to paragraph (8)(c), to a fine not exceeding $10,000.

12.—(1) Before making its recommendation on a restraining order, the Council must give all parties an opportunity to make submissions on any written and oral evidence given to the Council.
(2) The Council may require submissions to be made in writing or orally.

13.—(1) Subject to paragraph (2), in any proceedings on a restraining order —
(a)a restrained person (X) may authorise one or more persons to represent X; and
(b)the Minister may authorise one or more public officers to represent the Minister.
(2) An authorised representative or authorised officer —
(a)may be an advocate and solicitor within the meaning given by section 2(1) of the Legal Profession Act 1966; and
(b)must be a citizen of Singapore.
14. If any party does not appear before the Council when required to do so, the Council may, if satisfied that the party has been duly notified to appear, proceed without the party.

15.—(1) Subject to the Act and these Regulations, the Council may adopt any procedure that it considers just and efficient in reviewing a restraining order.
(2) The Council must avoid undue formality in its proceedings.
16. To avoid doubt, the Evidence Act 1893 and all other written laws relating to evidence do not apply to proceedings before the Council.

17.—(1) Before making its recommendation on a restraining order, the Council may give directions to cure or waive any failure to comply with any provision of these Regulations.
(2) However, a recommendation on a restraining order is not invalidated by any failure to comply with any provision of these Regulations.
(3) The chairperson may at any time correct a clerical mistake in any document recording any direction or proceedings under these Regulations.

heading.en: Recommendation of Council to be notified, etc.

text.en: 18. When the Council makes its recommendation on a restraining order, the secretary must without delay notify the parties of the recommendation.
